I have farmed this land my whole life. My family holds about 9 mu of contracted land here in Quzhou. My husband works construction in Shijiazhuang most of the year, so the fields are mine to manage. I know what this soil does, what the neighbors grow, what the seed store in town carries. I am not going to try anything new. New things lose money, and I cannot afford to lose money.

**My reasoning:**

I plant winter wheat and summer maize, same as always. Everyone here does this rotation — the land is flat, the well is close enough, and wheat gives us food security while maize brings in cash. I keep one small plot of garlic for household use and to sell a little locally. I will not plant cotton or vegetables on any scale because I cannot run after them alone. Wheat and maize I can manage with the tractor hire service and my son coming back for harvest week.

For seed, I buy the improved wheat variety from the county cooperative — 冀麦 series, whatever they have this year. For maize I use 郑单958 hybrid, everyone uses it, it is reliable. I know how much fertilizer I put down: base fertilizer before planting wheat, then one topdressing at jointing stage. Same for maize with a base application and one chase application. I probably use more urea than the extension station says I should — my neighbors do the same. Better to have enough than to watch the plants yellow.

Irrigation: I open the well four times for wheat. Water is getting harder to pump and the government says to cut back, but four times is already less than my mother used to do. For maize I try to get by on two irrigations and hope the summer rain helps.

I hire a rotary tiller for wheat land prep. For maize, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest — no time for deep plowing in June, the window is too short.
